spec.title: CPU Throttling Rate
spec.description: Package thermal throttling on the machines that own their CPUs. LXC guests are excluded: the counter reaches them from the shared kernel and describes the hypervisor, not the container. Only the Intel hypervisors report it -- pve is AMD and the Raspberry Pis are ARM, and neither exposes this counter.

spec.expr: 100 - (avg by (nodename) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)) * 100)

sort_desc(100 - (avg by (nodename) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)) * 100))

spec.title: Filesystem Usage
spec.description: Every filesystem in scope, fullest first. This is where the "Filesystems Over 85%" count in the Summary resolves to a name.

spec.expr: sort_desc((1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance=~"$instance",fstype=~"ext[234]|xfs|btrfs|zfs|vfat",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/docker/.*|/boot/efi|/boot/firmware"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance=~"$instance",fstype=~"ext[234]|xfs|btrfs|zfs|vfat",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/docker/.*|/boot/efi|/boot/firmware"}) * 100 * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info))

spec.title: Filesystems Over 85%
spec.description: Counts filesystems, not nodes: one host can have several, and on pve they share a ZFS pool. 85% is where NodeFilesystemSpaceFillingUp starts looking at the trend, so a non-zero count here is the level that alert needs before it will fire -- it is the earlier and weaker of the two signals, and does not by itself mean anything is alerting.

spec.expr: (node_load1{instance=~"$instance"} / on(instance) group_left() count by (instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$instance"})) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)

(node_load1{instance=~"$instance"} / on(instance) group_left() count by (instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$instance"})) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)

sort_desc((1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{instance=~"$instance"} / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{instance=~"$instance"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info) * 100)

up{job="scrapeConfig/monitoring/node-exporter-external", instance=~"$instance"} * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (last_over_time(node_uname_info{job="scrapeConfig/monitoring/node-exporter-external"}[1d]))

spec.title: Nodes Down
spec.description: Scrape targets not answering. Red from one, unlike the other tiles here: this is the only one that is a fault rather than a state.

spec.title: Nodes Over 80% Memory
spec.description: Counted at 80% because that is where capacityThresholds turns yellow everywhere else in this repo. 90% was tried and has not happened once in 30 days.

spec.title: Nodes Saturated
spec.description: Nodes whose 1-minute load average exceeds their CPU count, meaning work was queuing. Same quantity as the Load Average panels below and on node/k8s-node/proxmox-otlp, so a figure here can be compared with any of them.

spec.expr: count((node_load1{instance=~"$instance"} / on(instance) group_left() count by (instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$instance"})) > 1) or vector(0)

spec.title: Rebooted (1h)
spec.description: Nodes that booted within the last hour. Not a fault, but it explains gaps and resets elsewhere on this dashboard; a maintenance window showed 10 at once.

spec.expr: ((label_replace(node_thermal_zone_temp{type=~"x86_pkg_temp|cpu-thermal", instance=~"$instance"}, "sensor", "$1", "type", "(.*)")) or (label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{chip=~".*_0000:00:18_.*", sensor="temp1", instance=~"$instance"}, "sensor", "cpu", "", ""))) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)

spec.title: ZFS ARC Size
spec.description: Only nodes with a pool imported appear; see zfsActive in the source for how they are told apart from the ones that merely have the module loaded. A node that gains a pool will show up here on its own, with no change needed to this panel.

spec.expr: (node_zfs_arc_size{instance=~"$instance"} and on(instance) (node_zfs_arc_size{instance=~"$instance"} > 1024 * 1024)) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)
(node_zfs_arc_c_max{instance=~"$instance"} and on(instance) (node_zfs_arc_size{instance=~"$instance"} > 1024 * 1024)) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)
(node_zfs_arc_c_min{instance=~"$instance"} and on(instance) (node_zfs_arc_size{instance=~"$instance"} > 1024 * 1024)) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info)
